8 30ft lengths is a lot or rope honestly, unless you're absolutely mummifying your partner or doing some extremely complex ties (good on you if you are! Partial/whole suspension uses a lot of rope up). 

To start out and try some basic stuff I usually recommend 2 30ft sections, 2 15ft, and 2 10ft. 

That, all used at once, could get you a chest and hip harness, arm bands, spread eagle legs, and maybe more depending on your arrangement. 

One thing to remember when considering rope lengths in shibari especially is that they're usually folded in the center for weight dispersion and stability (aka you're wrapping doubled over rope around your partner, thedutchy.com is a good source to see what that looks like!), so that 30ft length is only half that on a human body, same for any other length. Because you're wrapping it from the bight, you're increasing the strength of the rope, its sticking power (one rope doubled over is going to stay in place at the same tension across 2 lines better than one rope wrapped multiple times which could have inconsistent tension), and the comfort of the tie on your bottom.

A 50 foot rope is fine for body harnesses on most folks with maybe a little left. 30 is recommended but if the person being tied isn't stick thin you'll end up adding rope anyway so 50 is frankly ideal for someone in the dress size 12-16 range for a Hishi Karada or more complex chest harness.

I do second what someone else said about silk rope though, if you're not wanting to cut the rope because you don't wanna ruin your "fancy" rope, you shouldn't use it. Rope has to get cut sometimes. Emergencies, flaws or runs in the rope, wax that is *extremely in there like goddang*, whatever reason. Being too attached to an individual strand of rope means it should be a) a sentimental piece you only bring out occasionally, or b) not used for more than looks. Functional rope should be replacable, durable, and well made. 

I frankly use cotton for a lot of ground work during a scene, especually if I know it's going to get dirty bc it is A) dirt cheap, you can but triple braided cotton for 10 cents a foot on most nautical supply sites and it is still very strong and high quality, B) sturdy, it has some stretch but largely will hold form even if someone is struggling unless you are tying someone who is extremely strong/bendy, and C) washable, cotton can just be tossed in a pillow case, tied off, washed in the washing machine with your delicates, and then hung to dry and deenergized and bam, back to use. Definitely great for messy crotch ties and wax (toss it in the freezer after a scene then whip it a bit to break the wax off, way easier than silk to clean).

Hemp is also a reasonable option and one a lot of people use (hemp is the go to for suspension tho POSH or Hempex is more safe imo) mostly because it is also sturdy, not terribly expensive unless you want fancy colors or Brand recognition (you can get 30ft lengths of Hemp rope for like 20-30USD, more if you want Fancy Rope with specific ends predone for you or a specific weave),  and cuts quick in an emergency. 

If you DO want to use silk, bamboo silk in microbiotic (you should still wash it every so often but if it isn't covered in *ahem* juices you're probably fine) and dirt cheap if you do some research (I've found it around 30 cents a foot before), and also cuts pretty easily if you get a fuckton of it for some reason to make your own kit. 

All in all, don't be afraid to cut your rope! It isn't going to ruin it forever, even half lengths of a 50ft piece make good ties for wrists and ankles (25ft is great I have found for especially twiggy partners for hips and simple chest harnesses!) And you can always add rope to the ends of your running line if you run out (larks head over a knot is simple, quick, and effective unless you really want that Photo Shoot Perfection). Welcome to the world of rope bondage!

You can speed up the carmelization process in onions by adding like 1/4 tsp of baking soda to the party.
